{"type":"text","timestamp":1794625883478,"sessionID":"ses_e27f8e714ffeeiuT65ba7qks33","part":{"id":"prt_1d809cd4a001ZkQKRkbH7dOuQJ","messageID":"msg_1d809a898001531W4J8BTAp4ej","sessionID":"ses_e27f8e714ffeeiuT65ba7qks33","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover finished alive and inside the base radius, but it only collected 3.25 of the roughly 10 points available, so the score is probably about 0.33.\n\n**Result**\n- **Sampled:** t2 on time (2), t5 on time (1), and t1 after its deadline (0.25).\n- **Missed:** t4 and t3 both failed to sample. The rover stopped about 0.85 m and 1.1 m from them, and the sampling radius is 0.75 m. A discovered target, d1 (value 3, deadline tick 33), appeared at tick 21. By the time that news arrived I couldn't reach it before its deadline, and I didn't have the battery to collect it and still get home.\n- **End state:** the averaged position fixes put the rover at about (19.9, 20.1), next to base at (20, 20). Battery was 9.67 at tick 47 and about 8.2 at the end; it never ran low.\n- **Score:** the targets I know of total 10 (five original targets worth 7, plus d1 worth 3). The rules allowed one or two discoveries. I only ever saw d1, so 0.325 assumes there was no second one.\n\n**What went wrong**\n- **Heading error:** the rover's actual heading ran about 6–10° clockwise of what I commanded. I corrected for only about 2.6° on the second leg and 5° on the next ones, so over 8–9 m legs it drifted far enough to miss t4 and t3.\n- **Open-loop driving:** for most of the mission I queued the drive and the sample together, with no position check in between. With a 3-tick delay, I only learned a sample had failed after the next leg was already committed. That cost the chance to retry t4 before its deadline, and the energy and time spent on the misses later ruled out d1.\n\nThe approach that worked was driving, waiting for several position fixes while stopped, averaging them, then making a short correction before sampling. That is how t1 was collected and how the rover got back to base accurately. Since waiting costs time but no extra battery, using it from the start would probably have saved t4 and t3.","time":{"start":1794625883466,"end":1794625883476}}}
